stories.title: Dhaka University keeps admission schedule despite UGC request
stories.summary: Dhaka University will retain its November 25 application deadline and December 5 test start date. The university ignored a request from the University Grants Commission to reconsider the timeline to accommodate students retaking Higher Secondary Certificate exams. The university has decided that the schedule will remain as planned.

stories.title: Public universities plan February admission tests
stories.summary: Public university vice-chancellors agreed to begin the 2026-27 admission process in January, with tests scheduled for February. The move aims to accommodate students passing upcoming Higher Secondary Certificate supplementary examinations. Universities will now coordinate to finalise specific dates for the entrance tests.

stories.title: GATE 2027 correction window open until November 14
stories.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology Madras has opened a correction window for GATE 2027 application forms. Candidates can rectify errors regarding their name, date of birth, exam city, or paper code. The facility is available for those who have already successfully submitted their initial applications.

stories.title: Quebec universities report international student decline
stories.summary: International student enrollment in Quebec universities fell by approximately 12 percent this fall, representing 5,900 fewer students. The decline marks a second consecutive year of double-digit drops. Only Bishop's University reported an increase in international numbers as the province considers changes to its language and health policies.

stories.summary: Rebellion Research has released its 2027 rankings for South Korean universities, prioritizing artificial intelligence offerings and financial resources per student. The firm claims these factors are frequently overlooked by traditional rankings, which it says rely too heavily on historical reputation and conventional prestige.

stories.title: University of Mysore ranks 247th in South Asia
stories.summary: The University of Mysore has secured the 247th position in the QS World University Rankings for South Asia. The institution attributed its performance to academic standards and international partnerships, despite noting a shortage of permanent teaching faculty. It remains the top-ranked state university in Karnataka.

stories.title: National Economics University targets top 150 global ranking
stories.summary: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung has tasked the National Economics University in Hanoi with reaching the world's top 150 universities by 2030. The institution, which celebrated its 70th anniversary this month, is also expected to achieve top 100 status by 2035 and international renown by 2045.

stories.title: FAU entrepreneurship program rises in rankings
stories.summary: Florida Atlantic University’s College of Business undergraduate entrepreneurship program is now ranked 14th by the Princeton Review and Entrepreneur Magazine, up from 19th last year. The graduate program holds the 43rd spot for 2027. The college credits its faculty for providing practical business experience.

stories.title: Galgotias University climbs 32 places in Asia rankings
stories.summary: Galgotias University has risen 32 places to 422nd in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027. While most of India’s highest-ranked institutions saw their positions decline this year, the university continues an upward trend. It is now ranked 104th in Southern Asia.

stories.title: Parul University enters Southern Asia rankings
stories.summary: Parul University has moved into the 791-800 band in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, up from the 1001-1100 band last year. The Gujarat-based institution also debuted at 239th in the Southern Asia sub-regional table, which utilizes the same data framework as the primary continental list.

stories.title: Michigan State University maintains employability ranking
stories.summary: Michigan State University is ranked 9th among U.S. public universities for graduate employability in the 2027 Times Higher Education report. The ranking highlights institutions that recruiters from leading companies believe best prepare students for the workplace. The university placed 33rd among all U.S. institutions.

stories.title: University of Houston entrepreneurship program tops list again
stories.summary: The University of Houston’s Wolff Center for Entrepreneurship has earned the No. 1 undergraduate ranking from the Princeton Review for eight consecutive years. The program reports that its students and alumni have launched 3,070 ventures and raised $1.23 billion in startup capital since 2016.

stories.title: Nottingham strike paused after new offer
stories.summary: University of Nottingham staff have paused a two-month strike following an improved offer from management regarding job cuts. The dispute involves a transformation plan that puts 560 roles at risk. The union stated the pause reflects progress but does not end the underlying dispute.

stories.title: Uber driver convicted of rape
stories.summary: A Montgomery County man has been convicted of raping a Villanova University student. The victim had ordered an Uber to her dormitory after feeling unwell in September 2024. The conviction follows court proceedings in Pennsylvania.

stories.title: Tuition fee plans face criticism
stories.summary: Critics have warned that Andy Burnham’s plan to subsidize tuition for European Union students could pressure university finances. The initiative is linked to a potential trade deal requiring fee parity for EU students. Ministers fear that without the agreement, UK manufacturing could lose access to European supply chains.

stories.title: UVA appoints new architecture dean
stories.summary: The University of Virginia has named Amy Catania Kulper as the next dean of its School of Architecture. Kulper, a historian and former leader at the Bartlett School of Architecture, will assume the role on January 6. She succeeds Malo Hutson, who is returning to the faculty.

stories.title: IIT-Bombay launches entrepreneurship diploma
stories.summary: IIT-Bombay has announced an e-Postgraduate Diploma in Innovation and Entrepreneurship. The 36-credit program, developed with Jaro Education, begins November 16. It focuses on venture creation and design thinking through practical projects, simulations, and pitch presentations intended to translate innovative ideas into sustainable business opportunities.

stories.title: Lithuanian student union reports discrimination
stories.summary: The Lithuanian National Union of Students has reported that international applicants are facing intimidation and discrimination during the admissions process. The union president told a parliamentary committee that some institutions are rejecting students based on their country of origin rather than their academic qualifications.

stories.title: VCU student develops healthcare guide for international peers
stories.summary: Doctor of Nursing Practice student Karma Choki has created a project to help international students navigate the U.S. healthcare system. Choki noted that students from countries with universal healthcare often struggle with the complexity of American medical services. Navigating the system is now part of the curriculum.

stories.title: IIT Madras Pravartak opens free online courses for schools
stories.summary: IIT Madras Pravartak and BodhBridge Education have launched free online training for students in Classes 7 to 12 and teachers. The courses cover topics including AI, electric vehicles, and classroom management. Registration for the November 2026 to January 2027 cohorts is now open on the programme portal.

stories.title: IIT Madras and BodhBridge expand free training offerings
stories.summary: IIT Madras Pravartak has partnered with BodhBridge to offer free online training for students and educators. The curriculum includes leadership development, career counselling, and student engagement. Applications are currently being accepted on the official website for those looking to add to their existing educational credentials.

stories.title: Smith College to close campus childcare center
stories.summary: Smith College will close its Fort Hill childcare center in June 2027. President Sarah Willie-LeBreton stated the move is not for budget relief, but to reallocate resources toward a childcare subsidy for up to 350 employees. The decision has prompted significant backlash from the campus community.

stories.title: Remembering Maulana Azad and the foundations of Indian education
stories.summary: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad served as India's first Education Minister from 1947 until 1958. During his tenure, the ministry oversaw the establishment of the first Indian Institute of Technology and the University Grants Commission. He managed these institutions while overseeing a national literacy rate of 18.33 percent.

stories.title: University of Melbourne to cut 179 staff
stories.summary: The University of Melbourne plans to cut 179 non-academic jobs following a $124 million operating deficit. The university described its financial results as disappointing and unsustainable, citing pressure from declining international student numbers. The institution has now recorded financial losses for five consecutive years.
